newsitem.title: USA: IBM price target raised by Merrill Lynch.
newsitem.headline: IBM price target raised by Merrill Lynch.

text.p: Merrill Lynch analyst Dan Mandresh said Friday he had raised his price target on International Business Machines Corp shares to about $195 over the next 12 months.
IBM shares were up 2-3/8 to 139-1/4 in heavy trading this morning.

Mandresh said he believes the company's current valuation will expand over the next 12 months, from its current P/E ratio of 10-11 times estimated 1997 earnings of $13 a share, to 13 times 1998 estimates of $15 a share.
This will result in a 12-month price objective of $195.
"Our preliminary checks into the current outlook for the fourth quarter indicate that things are on track to our forecast revenue growth of 10 percent, to $24 billion," Mandresh said in a report.
The month of December typically represents roughly 60 percent of the fourth quarter's shipments, he said.
"We believe IBM is on track in the U.S. to full-year growth of 10 percent, which fits our fourth quarter forecast of 13.8 percent -- the third quarter in a row of double-digit growth," Mandresh said.
He also said business is improving in Europe, giving encouragement to his cautious forecast of 2.5 percent revenue growth in Europe in the fourth quarter.
